thread.title: Cracks surface in the bull trend, S&P 500 nails major support

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Cracks surface in the bull trend, S&P 500 nails major support
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Market cross currents have surfaced to start October against the backdrop of rising interest rates and energy prices.
Consider that the Nasdaq Composite has violated key trendline support — plunging to two-month lows — while the S&P 500 has effectively nailed its former breakout point (2,873), thus far preserving a bullish bias.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, -0.14% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
See Also How Y7 Studio's CEO turned her yoga side hustle into a business × As illustrated, the S&P has thus far maintained major support.
The familiar area matches the breakout point, broadly spanning from 2,863 to 2,873. Monday’s low (2,862) closely matched support and was punctuated by a close (2,884) near session highs.
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average remains comparably stronger.
In its case, the index has maintained its range bottom (26,349) rising from a fleeting downturn to nearly three-week lows. The prevailing rally attempt’s quality remains an open question.
Against this backdrop, the Nasdaq Composite COMP, +0.03% remains the weakest of the big three U.S. benchmarks.
Recall that it started October with a failed breakout attempt, topping two points under its record close (8,109).
The index has subsequently plunged as much as 453 points,or 5.6% from the range top, reaching two-month lows. Technical damage has been inflicted, and is better illustrated below.
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has violated four notable technical levels. Specifically:
Trendline support pinned to the April low. The former breakout point, matching the July peak of 7,933. The 50-day moving average, currently 7,922. The September low of 7,874. Put differently, the Nasdaq has violated trendline support and concurrently notched a “lower low” vs. the September low. The tandem events signal an intermediate-term trend shift.
Tactically, the breakdown point pivots to resistance (7,874) and an eventual close higher would place the brakes on bearish momentum.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average remains comparably resilient.
As illustrated, the index has maintained its range bottom (26,350) and is positioned comfortably atop the 50-day moving average.
On further weakness, a deeper floor matches the August peak (26,168).
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has effectively nailed its breakout point.
To reiterate, the specific area broadly spans from 2,863 to 2,873. Monday’s session low (2,862) matched support, and was punctuated by a bullish reversal to close near session highs.
The bigger picture As detailed above, technical cross currents have surfaced to start October.
On a headline basis, the Nasdaq Composite has violated trendline support — signaling an intermediate-term trend shift — while the comparably resilient S&P 500 has maintained major support, preserving a bullish bias.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF has turned lower amid a sustained October volume spike.
In the process, the small-cap benchmark has tagged its 200-day moving average, currently 161.05, for the first time since May. The IWM has not closed under the 200-day since August 2017.
Tactically, initial resistance matches the former range bottom (162.26) and a close higher would mark a step toward stabilization.
Similarly, the SPDR S&P MidCap 400 has extended its violation of trendline support.
Recall that notable floors match the bottom of the January gap (357.90) and the 200-day moving average, currently 355.30.
Monday’s session low (355.35) registered just above the 200-day moving average, punctuating a successful retest. Separately, last week’s close (357.87) and Monday’s close (357.97) have closely matched support.
Combined, the small- and mid-cap benchmarks have thus far maintained the 200-day moving average, and the quality of the prevailing rally attempt may be a useful bull-bear gauge.
Meanwhile, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 SPY, -0.15% remains comparably stronger.
Still, the SPY has turned lower amid increased volume to retest the 50-day moving average, currently 287.87. Slightly deeper support matches the September low (286.71) an area the SPY has thus far maintained, outpacing the S&P 500.
Summing up the backdrop All told, the widely-tracked U.S. benchmarks have diverged. The October downdraft has inflicted material damage to the small- and mid-cap benchmarks as well as the Nasdaq Composite.
Against this backdrop, the more representative S&P 500 Index remains comparably resilient.
Still, the S&P has reached a headline technical test that remains underway.
To start, an inflection point matches the 50-day moving average, currently 2,880, a level that has underpinned the S&P on a closing basis since July 5.
This is followed by the more important breakout point, broadly spanning from 2,863 to 2,873.
The S&P 500 has thus far bottomed at 2,862 — effectively matching support — and the quality of its prevailing rally attempt will likely add color.
Tactically, an eventual violation of the breakout point would mark a “lower low” — combined with a break below the 50-day moving average — raising the flag to an intermediate-term trend shift. The S&P 500’s intermediate-term bias remains bullish pending such a move.
See also: Charting a bullish Q4 start, S&P 500 rises to challenge record close.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Interest rates and energy prices take flight to start Q4 Drilling down further, broad-market headwinds have surfaced to start the fourth quarter. Two headline technical events remain in play.
To start, the 10-year Treasury note yield TNX, -0.77% has taken flight, reaching seven-year highs.
Technically, the prevailing upturn has resolved a double bottom defined by the July and August lows. Its projected target (3.21) from the pattern has been nominally surpassed.
More broadly, the yield has likely asserted a higher plateau, underpinned by the breakout point (3.11). (Also recall the 30-year note yield’s breakout, detailed last week. )
Meanwhile, the United States Oil Fund USO, +0.89% has also broken out. The fund tracks the price of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) light, sweet crude oil.
Here again, the shares started October with a bang, knifing to three-year highs.
The breakout opens the path to less-charted territory, illustrated on the four-year chart , and potentially material longer-term follow-through. An intermediate-term target continues to project to the 17.10 area.
Combined, interest rates and energy prices have surged to start the fourth quarter, and the tandem breakouts have inflicted collateral damage to the U.S. sub-sector backdrop.
Sources of sector weakness Moving to U.S. sectors, familiar sources of weakness stand out.
To start, the SPDR S&P Homebuilders ETF XHB, -2.87% has extended its technical breakdown, plunging to 18-month lows.
The downturn originates from trendline resistance, and punctuates a violation of the 50-day moving average, a recent inflection point.
Tactically, the breakdown point, circa 38.50, pivots to major resistance, and a close higher would mark a step toward stabilization. The group’s initial retest would be expected to draw sellers.
Similarly, the SPDR S&P Retail ETF XRT, +0.00% is off to a bearish October start.
Fundamentally, the group has been pressured amid rising interest rates and oil prices. Both reduce consumer discretionary spending capacity.
Separately, Amazon’s decision to increase its employees’ minimum wage to $15 per hour has pressured the retail sector amid concerns the group’s payroll costs may rise to compete.
Technically, the group has violated its breakout point, plunging on increased volume to the 200-day moving average, currently 47.75. As always, the 200-day is a widely-tracked longer-term trending indicator, with a posture higher signaling a primary uptrend. The quality of the group’s rally from support is worth tracking.
Sources of sector strength Conversely, familiar sources of sub-sector strength are intact. Quickly consider the following:
To start, the transports continue to act relatively well technically.
Though the iShares Transportation Average ETF IYT, -1.87% has edged under the 50-day moving average, it’s thus far maintained major support matching the June peak. Moreover, the tame October downturn has been punctuated by Monday’s bullish single-day reversal amid a volume spike.
Meanwhile, the Industrial Select Sector SPDR XLI, -1.54% has sustained a break to eight-month highs.
The group’s orderly two-week range is a continuation pattern, positioning it to build on the September breakout.
Looking elsewhere, the Health Care Select Sector SPDR’s XLV, +0.17% backdrop comfortably remains bullish.
The group’s persistent third-quarter uptrend — see July through September — has been punctuated by a modest downturn to start the fourth quarter. Though fueled by increased volume, limited technical damage has been inflicted.
Perhaps not surprisingly, the energy sectors are acting well amid surging crude oil prices.
In this case, the VanEck Vectors Oil Servcies ETF OIH, +1.17% has cleared trendline resistance, rising to challenge the 200-day moving average. The group’s tight October range, amid a down market, lays the groundwork for a potential breakout.
Influential sectors in flux Moving to the gray areas, two influential groups are in flux — the financials and technology sector.
To start, the Financial Select Sector XLF, -0.39% has staged an October upturn , rising amid the prevailing Treasury-yield breakout.
Still, the lukewarm rally has stalled near the 50- and 200-day moving averages. Tactically, the group’s prevailing backdrop supports a neutral bias. The pending break from its range will likely add color.
Meanwhile, the Powershares QQQ Trust QQQ, +0.32% tracks the Nasdaq 100 Index and serves as a large-cap technology proxy.
Its recent price action registers as distinctly technical.
The QQQ tagged a record high (187.53) to start October, eclipsing its former record peak by one penny. The subsequent strong-volume downturn punctuates a violation of trendline support and the September low (180.44).
Tactically, the aggressive downturn raises the flag to an intermediate-term trend shift. The breakdown point (180.44) pivots to resistance, and a reversal higher would stabilize the backdrop. The initial retest is already underway, and will likely add color.
Summing up the sub-sector backdrop Collectively, the U.S. sub-sector backdrop remains bullish-leaning, on balance, though pockets of technical damage have been inflicted. The still rotational backdrop is worth tracking for incremental deterioration.
